report.source_text: Treatment commenced, including high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine and rituximab, followed by radiotherapy (40 Gy total). Repeat MRI showed significant improvement in the central nervous system disease (figure 1G–I) and she also improved functionally, being discharged home without a package of care after previously needing 24 h nursing care. Ten months later, functional status had not deteriorated and neuropsychometric testing was equivalent to that done several months prior to commencement of treatment (ie, before significant further cognitive decline), however remaining below premorbid estimates. Importantly, her gait and mobility also improved dramatically as she went from being unable to walk unaided immediately prior to treatment, to walking independently, swimming twice weekly and using a cross-trainer regularly.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Primary central nervous system diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (lymphomatosis cerebri pattern)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old previously healthy woman presented with subacute 3-week progressive amnestic syndrome, personality change, emotional lability, and focal neurological deficits (expressive/receptive aphasia, ideational/ideomotor apraxia). MRI brain demonstrated extensive confluent T2 hyperintensity throughout the cerebrum and brainstem without mass effect, abnormal enhancement, or diffusion restriction, consistent with lymphomatosis cerebri. CSF analysis showed elevated protein (0.74 g/L) with normal glucose and cell count, negative viral PCRs, and negative cytology for atypical cells. Months after presentation, brain biopsy revealed diffuse and nodular infiltration by large atypical lymphoid cells with perivascular clustering, confirmed as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Systemic staging with bone marrow biopsy and PET/CT excluded extracerebral disease, establishing primary CNS lymphoma. Treatment with high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine, rituximab, and radiotherapy (40 Gy) resulted in significant radiographic improvement and functional recovery, with independent ambulation and stable neurocognitive status at 10-month follow-up.
